title: Pet Shop
story: A pet shop has dogs, cats, fish, and birds — but each animal needs different info. A dog has a breed, a cat has a fur color, a fish needs a tank size, and a bird may or may not talk. You need one type that handles all four.
why: Enum variants with data let one type represent completely different shapes of information.
analogy: An enum with data is like a package with a label and contents. The label says "Dog" and inside is the breed. Open the package with `match` to see what's inside.
try_it: Add a `Hamster(fur_type: Str)` variant to the Pet enum. Update `describe` and `needs_cage` (hamsters need cages). Create a hamster named "Fluffy" and print its description.
tips: Each variant can have different types and numbers of fields — they're independent
Use `_` as a wildcard in match to match any variant without caring about its data
Match arms use `=>` followed by a block `{ }` for multi-line logic
common_mistakes: Treating all variants as having the same data — you can't access `breed` on a Fish
Forgetting the `_` wildcard on data you don't use — write `Bird(_)` not `Bird(can_talk)` if unused
